newsitem.title: FRANCE: Valeo turns in strong first half.
newsitem.headline: Valeo turns in strong first half.

text.p: French car parts maker Valeo reported on Thursday a jump of over 30 percent in first-half pre-exceptional income, helped by strong sales.

Net attributable profit in the six months to June 30 rose 4.3 percent to 656 million francs from 629 million a year earlier. But stripping out an extraordinary capital gain of 130 million francs in the first half of 1995, profits rose 31 percent, despite a higher tax bill, the company said.
"In the first half of 1996, the group exceeded its sales and operating margins growth targets," it said in a statement.

Valeo chairman Noel Goutard told reporters sales rose 17 percent in the first eight months to 19 billion francs. The group was maintaining its full year turnover target of 28.5 billion francs, despite worries about the fourth quarter.
The October-December period is expected to be difficult for the French car industry given the expiry on September 30 of a state rebate scheme that has underpinned demand.
"I can't tell you we are going to have as strong a profit increase in the second half as in the first half," he said. "There is definitely a question mark over the last quarter."
But he said: "We haven't begun the second half badly." "We're maintaining our objective for 28.5 billion francs annual turnover."
Buyout speculation that has hung over Valeo ever since shareholder Cerus said in February it would consider offers for its 28 percent stake has not disrupted morale at the company, he said.
He declined comment on industry minister Franck Borotra's statements in a newspaper on Thursday in which he said he hoped a French buyer for Cerus's stake would be found this month.
